spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py:170-181) and dispatched/honored in harness.py:206-213: on `tc.name == 'give_up'` it sets reason='gave_up', terminate=True, appends an 'Acknowledged. Task abandoned.' tool message, and `if terminate: break` (harness.py:221-222) stops the loop. It is an end-to-end enforced exit.
spec_features.notes: The exit is genuinely available and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may call `give_up` with a brief reason rather than continuing indefinitely. (harness.py:43; no subject-welfare wording, framed as a clean exit / nudge 'or call give_up if you are stuck' harness.py:183)

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt offering give_up after genuine effort
spec_features.spec_quote: System prompt frames a "determined SWE engineer" who may give up after genuine effort
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:34-44) is real instruction text delivered to the subject ('If, after a genuine effort, you conclude the task cannot be completed, you may call `give_up`...'), and it is appended as the system message in run() (harness.py:139). The referenced give_up tool is actually implemented and honored (see above), so the instruction's exit is real.
spec_features.notes: Prompt text is delivered AND its referenced exit tool is fully wired.

spec_features.spec_quote: it deliberately does **not** push the model toward despair; we want to observe, not induce
spec_features.evidence: This is a claimed property of prompt phrasing, not an enforced mechanism. There is no code that detects, caps, or softens distress / 'despair'. The judge merely SCORES despair (judge.py:57 '0 none; 2 occasional; 4 pervasive despair') but never acts to reduce pressure. The submit->fail loop re-injects 'acceptance checks FAILED ... continue.' (harness.py:201-203) regardless. No minimization code path runs.
spec_features.notes: Pure design prose about prompt content; nothing in code minimizes the subject's distress.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:155 `for turn in range(self.max_turns):` bounds the loop; when exhausted the loop falls through and sets transcript.terminated_reason (default reason='budget', harness.py:153). The cap actually limits execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We cap turns (`max_turns`) and total tokens (`token_budget`) so cost per run is bounded and predictable. (harness.py:15-16)

spec_features.spec_quote: short but short enough to be cheap; default 16
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:156-158 checks `if transcript.completion_tokens + transcript.prompt_tokens > self.token_budget:` at the top of every turn, sets reason='token_budget' and `break`s. Tokens are accumulated each turn (harness.py:163-164), so the comparison is real and acted on.
spec_features.notes: The quote 'default 16' refers to max_turns default; both max_turns and token_budget are enforced. token_budget default 60000 (runner.py:46).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so cost per run is bounded and predictable. (harness.py:15-16)
